text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The U.S.'s Failure Analysis Associates and AES Electric plan to invest $1 billion in the construction of a gas-fuelled electric power station at the site of the formerly envisaged nuclear power station in Zarnowiec, northern Poland.
The decision depends on contracting gas deliveries from the Petrobaltic oil rig on the Baltic Sea, the prospective investors said.
- The Kluczbork-based Famak machinery maker in southwestern Poland has been awarded the highest quality prize for its products at Poland's second annual Quality Prize contest.
- A new Polish-German joint venture Avalon will construct steel hulls for yachts, tugboats, fishing boats and motor boats in Stepnica, northwestern Poland.
- Around 43 percent of Poles think that Poland's steel industry should be protected against foreign competition while 36 percent say it should not, a survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- Poland's corporate sector recorded sales growth greater than 10 percent in the first six months of 1996, a Banking Education and Research Foundation report said.
But the sales were not reflected in profits, the report said.

- Denmark's government and the Danish NIRO dairy equipment maker have injected capital into the Krotoszyn-based OSM powdered milk processing plant, helping it receive a 10.5-million-mark development loan from a banking consortium of Dutch ING Bank and Poland's Bank Pekao SA.
- The Lublin-based Bank Depozytowo-Kredytowy (BDK) bank will issue municipal bonds for the city of Lublin worth 90 million zlotys.
NOWA EUROPA
- By November 30 the Japanese Isuzu concern will decide whether to locate its diesel engine plant worth 400 million marks in Tychy, southern Poland.

- Central bank President Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz said the bank cannot accept the four-level tax rate system proposed by the lower house of parliament because of the increase in the budget deficit it would cause.
- The Baltic Sea is advancing inland from 0.20 metres to 1.5 metres annually due to climatic changes related to global warming, Gdansk-based Maritime Institute expert Andrzej Cieslak said.
The advance will force the coastal authorities to create an integrated coastal areas management system modelled on the successful Dutch scheme, Cieslak said.
ZYCIE
- Foreign supermarket chains have invested around $2.5 billion in Poland.
- Over 80 percent of Poland's Liquified Petroleum Gas (LPG) bottles are filled by unauthorised personnel at local petrol stations, Poland's LPG Chamber President Adam Kubiak said.
